Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka bowled well on Day 3. The spinners were consistent with their line and length and got the reward however it got a bit frustrating in the end as they had to work hard for that final wicket. New Zealand on the other hand will be happy with how they have batted. Tom Latham gave them a blistering start, Kane Williamson followed and kept troubling the Lankan bowlers. Daryl Mitchell then notched up his fifty but once he fell the onus was on Phillips to score as many as possible with wickets tumbling at the other end. It feels New Zealand will be more than happy with how their hard-hitting batter has performed with the tail enders. Right then! New Zealand lead by 35 runs. The cracks have opened up and it won't surprise if New Zealand use spinners straightaway. Sri Lanka have to show a lot of character now. Let's see how they bat.

Glenn Phillips' excellent innings has helped New Zealand lead by 35 runs. At one stage, it felt New Zealand would only be able to match their first innings score as they kept on losing wickets on a pitch which have opened up considerably. However, Glenn Phillips played a little cameo of immense maturity with not more than two wickets in hand to help them get ahead in the game.

Welcome to the action of Day 3 between Sri Lanka and New Zealand. The match is moving in some pace as after Day 2, the game is equally balanced and feels whoever dominates the ‘moving day’ will certainly have a chance to win the match. Sri Lanka scored 305 runs as they failed to add much to the overnight score of Day 1. The first session of Day 2 saw just 5 overs being bowled, thanks to the unwanted rain at Galle but after that there was plenty of action and we saw the Kiwi batters come out with a lot of intent. They scored at brisk pace with Latham taking the charge up front. Williamson then scored a fine fifty with Ravindra who looked well set but got out in quick succession along with Williamson to Dhananjaya de Silva. The Kiwis have a lot of batting left and still are 50 runs behind. Sri Lanka will hope they bowl some tight lines and lengths and put some pressure on the batters. An intersection first session is coming up. Stay tuned.

The Lankan bowlers had to toil hard, there was not a lot on offer for them from the wicket but their bowlers weren't at their best too. The wicket though has started playing tricks now and they'll hope their bowlers can take advantage of it. That wicket of Latham will give them a lot of confidence. Can they take control of the game after the break? We will find out. Join us for the last session in a bit.

The Kiwis did lose Latham right towards the end but they'll be pretty pleased with where they are in the game at the moment! Yes, they would have loved to be just the one down at the end of the break but credit to them for the way they batted throughout the session. First Conway and Latham put up a good stand. Conway fell but Latham continued. He scored a fine half ton. Williamson too is going along well. Just as it seemed the Kiwis would enter the break just the one down, they lost Latham towards the end. They'll now hope the batter coming in can continue the good work and they can pile on another good stand.
